title: Tube End Forming Machines — Expand & Reduce | NovoTech
meta_description: Hydraulic tube end formers that expand or reduce pipe ends to Ø3-1/2″ × 14 ga in one station — exhaust slip joints, sleeves, telescoping tube. Tooling included.
intro: A tube end former (pipe end forming machine) expands or reduces the end of a tube so two tubes slip together: an expanded end takes the next tube inside it, a reduced end fits into the next tube. İşitan's SFF single-station hydraulic end formers do both with one tooling set — the SFF 90-1 expands Ø1-3/8″ to 3-1/2″ and reduces down from Ø5/16″ in 14 ga mild steel with a 15 HP power unit, the SFF 60-1 covers tube to Ø2-3/8″ with 10 HP — for exhaust slip joints, handrail and fence sleeves, telescoping tube, furniture connectors and HVAC spigots. One forming set in the size you request is included and swaps in minutes; with CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON.

faq.q: Expanding or reducing — what does the end former do?
faq.a: An expander opens a tube end so the next tube slips inside (exhaust slip joints, telescoping handrail, sleeves); a reducer collapses the end to fit into the next tube. The SFF does both in one station with a hydraulic ram and interchangeable forming tools — one set is included, others are quoted to your tube size.

faq.q: What tube sizes and wall thickness can the SFF form?
faq.a: The SFF 90-1 expands tube from Ø1-3/8″ to Ø3-1/2″ and reduces ends down to Ø5/16″, in mild steel up to 14 ga; the SFF 60-1 covers tube to Ø2-3/8″. Stainless and thicker walls are quoted case by case — send us the tube OD, wall and the finished end size you need.

faq.q: How long does a tool change take?
faq.a: A few minutes: the forming set is held in a quick-change holder on the ram and the clamp. Most customers keep one set per tube size and swap between batches.

faq.q: Can the SFF do an exhaust slip joint?
faq.a: Yes — that is its most common job: expand one end of the pipe so the next section slides in, or reduce it to slip into a muffler or flex pipe. Expansion depth and the finished diameter are set by the tooling.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
